title: Functions I previously turned off keep turning themselves back on.

judgment.rationale: The live Needs-Author-Feedback label remains, and the existing triage comment directly asks the original author for concrete reproduction steps. The author has not replied; later comments are from other users and do not satisfy that request. The supplied diagnostic archive was rejected by the triage service as oversized, so its contents were not available for analysis.
evidence: The body says features disabled in PowerToys 0.101.2362 from Microsoft Store return to on after a few days; it says the reporter mainly uses Always on top and includes two screenshots plus a diagnostic ZIP link.
The triage bot requested concrete reproduction steps at 2026-10-09T16:17:31Z and said the archive could not be safely analyzed because an entry was oversized.
Two later comments from other users corroborate resets after installation/reboots; neither is a response from the original author.
The issue remains open with Needs-Author-Feedback; no matching fork issue or PR was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Wait for the original reporter to provide the requested repeatable steps; do not repeat the existing request or infer that other users' comments satisfy it.

fix_assessment.rationale: The symptom is plausible, but the trigger and affected module states remain too vague to identify a supportable code-level fix. The existing diagnostic archive was rejected; re-triage after the original author supplies the requested reproduction details.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says some disabled features, including tools beyond Always on top, return to enabled after a few days. A request for concrete steps is pending; replies from other users confirm similar behavior but do not establish this reporter's trigger.
known_information: The reporter identifies PowerToys 0.101.2362 from Microsoft Store and says they mainly use Always on top.
The report includes two screenshot attachments and a linked diagnostic ZIP; an automated triage comment says the archive was rejected as oversized and could not be analyzed.
The body only says randomly; the triage bot requested concrete reproduction steps. The original author has not responded, while two other users report similar resets around installation or reboots.
The live Needs-Author-Feedback label remains present.

The two attached screenshots show the Settings module list and current on/off states (including Always on top enabled); they do not establish which modules had been disabled before the reported reset.
inferences: Other reporters make the symptom plausible, but their replies cannot identify which modules changed or when this reporter's state changed.
The available evidence is insufficient to distinguish persisted setting loss, a startup/update transition, policy enforcement, or another trigger.
issue_context.analysis: The screenshots identify current module states but not which states changed or when. A previous targeted author request is already outstanding and the original author has not supplied the requested repro. Repeating it or requesting generic diagnostics would add no value; retain author-wait status until the author explains the sequence and affected module states.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body, screenshot references, all comments, labels, and existing bot request. The diagnostic ZIP was not downloaded or inspected; the public triage result says analysis was rejected due to an oversized entry.

Inspected Settings.UI.Library/EnabledModules.cs and GeneralSettings.cs plus runner/general_settings.cpp: per-module states are persisted, and configured Group Policy can override a requested state, but no evidence ties either to this report.
Checked live fork issue and PR searches for #51155; no matching fork mirror or fix attempt was found.
Viewed both screenshots: they document the current module-toggle list but not a before/after change or the event that re-enabled anything.

information_gaps.information: Concrete ordered steps and timing for one recurrence, including which modules were disabled and which returned to enabled.
information_gaps.why_needed: This identifies the affected settings and whether the transition follows an update, restart, or runtime event before code-level triage.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply to the existing triage request with the sequence from disabling the module(s) through observing the reset, and note the PowerToys version and any update/restart immediately before it.
